microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.
microphone.exampleUsage: The microphone was used during the activity.

mixing-console.definition: A control surface used to combine, adjust, and route several audio signals.
mixing-console.exampleUsage: The engineer adjusted microphone levels on the mixing console.

monitor-speaker.definition: A speaker used in a studio so producers or presenters can accurately hear an audio signal.
monitor-speaker.exampleUsage: The monitor speaker played the program audio in the control room.

transmitter.definition: Equipment that sends a radio, television, or communication signal over a distance.

antenna.definition: A device that sends or receives radio and television signals.
antenna.exampleUsage: The antenna was used during the activity.

amplifier.definition: A device that makes an audio signal stronger.
amplifier.exampleUsage: The amplifier was used during the activity.

equalizer.definition: A control that adjusts different ranges of sound frequencies.

compressor.definition: An electronic device that reduces the dynamic range of an audio signal.
compressor.exampleUsage: The compressor was used during the activity.

pop-filter.definition: A screen that reduces popping sounds when someone speaks into a microphone.

sound-booth.definition: A small enclosed room designed to reduce outside noise during recording or broadcasting.
sound-booth.exampleUsage: The presenter recorded the announcement in the sound booth.

acoustic-panel.definition: A panel designed to absorb or control sound reflections in a room.
acoustic-panel.exampleUsage: Acoustic panels reduced echoes in the studio.

on-air-sign.definition: A sign that indicates a live broadcast or recording is currently in progress.
on-air-sign.exampleUsage: The on-air sign lit up when the broadcast began.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.
computer.exampleUsage: The computer was used during the activity.

script-stand.definition: A stand or holder that supports a script where a presenter can read it easily.
script-stand.exampleUsage: The announcer placed the script on the script stand.

water-glass.definition: A thick solution of sodium silicate, also called water glass, can bind materials like cement. It can coat surfaces for protection and preserve eggs.

cable-management.definition: The organization, routing, and securing of cables to keep a workspace orderly and reduce tangles.
cable-management.exampleUsage: Good cable management kept the studio floor clear.

audio-interface.definition: A device that converts audio between microphones or instruments and a computer for recording or playback.
audio-interface.exampleUsage: The microphone connected to the computer through an audio interface.

digital-recorder.definition: An electronic device that records sound as digital audio files.
digital-recorder.exampleUsage: The reporter used a digital recorder for the interview.

sound-card.definition: Computer hardware that processes audio input and output.
sound-card.exampleUsage: The computer's sound card handled audio playback.

phantom-power.definition: Electrical power sent through some professional audio cables to operate compatible microphones and devices.
phantom-power.exampleUsage: The studio diagram labels phantom power as a microphone-powering feature.

xlr-cable.definition: A balanced audio cable with circular multi-pin connectors commonly used for professional microphones and audio equipment.
xlr-cable.exampleUsage: The microphone used an XLR cable.

headphone-amplifier.definition: A device that boosts and distributes audio signals for one or more sets of headphones.
headphone-amplifier.exampleUsage: The headphone amplifier supplied separate monitoring outputs.

audio-software.definition: Computer programs used to record, edit, mix, manage, or play sound.
audio-software.exampleUsage: The producer edited the interview in audio software.

waveform.definition: The shape of a wave illustrated graphically by plotting the values of the period quantity against time.

playback-button.definition: A control that starts playing recorded audio or video.
playback-button.exampleUsage: The producer pressed the playback button to review the segment.

record-button.definition: A control that starts recording audio, video, or data.
record-button.exampleUsage: The record button lit up when the interview began.

playlist.definition: A list of musical selections for performance or for broadcast by radio.

jingle.definition: A short, catchy tune used in an advertisement or show.

sound-effect.definition: A created or changed sound added to a film, show, game, or other media to reinforce what viewers see or what the story conveys.

station-id.definition: A short announcement or audio element that identifies a radio station.
station-id.exampleUsage: The station ID played at the top of the hour.

commercial-break.definition: A scheduled pause in a program during which advertisements are broadcast.
commercial-break.exampleUsage: The presenter returned after the commercial break.

news-bulletin.definition: A brief, formal report on radio or television gives the public clear, direct updates about current events.

weather-update.definition: A short broadcast giving recent weather conditions or forecast information.
weather-update.exampleUsage: The station aired a weather update before the news.

traffic-report.definition: A broadcast report about road conditions, congestion, or travel delays.
traffic-report.exampleUsage: The traffic report mentioned a major road closure.

interview-segment.definition: A section of a program devoted to questions and answers with a guest.
interview-segment.exampleUsage: The interview segment lasted ten minutes.

music-block.definition: A scheduled section of radio programming containing several songs or pieces of music.
music-block.exampleUsage: The music block followed the morning news.

radio-host.definition: A presenter who introduces and leads a radio program.
radio-host.exampleUsage: The radio host introduced the guest.

dj.definition: A person who announces and plays popular recorded music.

producer.definition: The person who organises the people, money, and work for a program.

sound-engineer.definition: A person who records, mixes, and improves the program’s sound.
sound-engineer.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Sound Engineer" in an educational description.

news-anchor.definition: A broadcaster who presents a news program, introduces its reports, and reads the main headlines on television or radio.

traffic-reporter.definition: A broadcaster who gives information about road and traffic conditions.
traffic-reporter.exampleUsage: The traffic reporter described delays on the highway.

weather-presenter.definition: A broadcaster who presents weather information and forecasts.
weather-presenter.exampleUsage: The weather presenter explained the weekend forecast.

sales-manager.definition: A manager responsible for leading sales staff and achieving sales goals, such as advertising sales at a station.
sales-manager.exampleUsage: The sales manager met with the advertising team.

program-director.definition: A faculty member or administrator who leads an academic program, guiding its plans, activities, and daily operation.

intern.definition: A student or trainee working temporarily to gain experience.

radio-receiver.definition: An electronic device that receives radio signals and converts them into sound or data.
radio-receiver.exampleUsage: The radio receiver was tuned to the local station.

car-radio.definition: A radio receiver installed in a vehicle.
car-radio.exampleUsage: The car radio displayed the station frequency.

portable-radio.definition: A small radio that can be carried and used away from a fixed power outlet, often using batteries.
portable-radio.exampleUsage: The portable radio played the emergency broadcast.

smartphone-app.definition: A software application designed to run on a smartphone.
smartphone-app.exampleUsage: The station's smartphone app streams its programs.

podcast.definition: A digital audio file made available on the Internet for downloading to a computer or portable media player.

streaming.definition: (computer science) using or relating to a form of continuous tape transport.

frequency-dial.definition: A control used to select or display a radio frequency.
frequency-dial.exampleUsage: The frequency dial showed the selected station.

volume-knob.definition: A control on an electronic device used to raise or lower the loudness of its audio output.
volume-knob.exampleUsage: The volume knob was used during the activity.

tuner.definition: An electronic receiver that detects and demodulates and amplifies transmitted signals.

turntable.definition: A circular horizontal platform that rotates a phonograph record while it is being played.

soundproof-booth.definition: An enclosed recording space designed to greatly reduce the transmission of outside sound.
soundproof-booth.exampleUsage: The voice actor recorded inside the soundproof booth.

on-air-light.definition: A light that turns on to show that a studio is broadcasting or recording live.

control-room.definition: A room where staff monitor and control a television broadcast.

recording-booth.definition: A small acoustically treated room designed for recording voice or sound.
recording-booth.exampleUsage: The singer recorded a short station jingle in the recording booth.

cue-card.definition: A card displaying prompts or text that helps a presenter remember what to say or do next.
cue-card.exampleUsage: The producer held up a cue card.

script.definition: The written words that presenters read during a broadcast.

frequency.definition: The number of times a radio wave repeats each second.

channel.definition: A television service or a numbered path for a signal.

commercial.definition: A short advertisement shown between television programs to promote a product or service.

interview.definition: A conversation in which one person asks another questions.
